summary: Komainu, a regulated digital asset services provider and custodian backed by Laser Digital and Blockstream, has completed the two-way transfer of a portfolio of digital assets with First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB) through the institutional digital asset custody framework the two firms have established. The transfers settled instantly.
content: Regulated digital asset custodian Komainu has successfully completed two-way digital asset transfers with First Abu Dhabi Bank. The transactions were executed using an established institutional digital asset custody framework between the two firms, resulting in instant settlement. Komainu is backed by major industry players including Laser Digital and Blockstream, expanding its footprint in institutional digital asset services.

Zilch Partners With Spotify to Offer Zilch Plus Members Up to Four Months of Spotify Premium Free
summary:
Zilch, the smarter spending platform, has announced a new partnership with Spotify, offering Zilch Plus members up to four months of Spotify Premium completely free – one of the best free trials for Zilch users to explore all that Spotify Premium has to offer.
The offer is available from today to all Zilch Plus members, with new Spotify Premium subscribers eligible for the full four-month trial. Returning Spotify Premium customers who haven't had Premium for two years can get their first two months at up to 75% off. Subject to availability. T&Cs apply.
The partnership marks the latest addition to Zilch's new membership programme, launched in August 2026 as part of the company's most significant product expansion to date. Zilch Plus, priced at £4.99 per month, offers members up to 6% back in rewards on debit spending alongside a growing range of exclusive member benefits.
Andreas Andreou, Chief Revenue Officer at Zilch, said: “Zilch Plus was built around the idea that our most engaged customers deserve more from every pound they spend. Partnering with Spotify to offer one of the best free trials on the market is exactly the kind of benefit that brings that to life.”
Martin Garph Kirsch, Head of Distribution Partnerships at Spotify, added: “Spotify Premium gives listeners more of what they love, with ad-free music, offline downloads and higher-quality audio, all in one place. We’re delighted to partner with Zilch to bring those benefits to their community of engaged members.”
Find out more about Zilch’s Spotify offer here: https://www.zilch.com/uk/spotify

LendInvest Selects Pepper Advantage’s PRISM Platform for Next Growth Phase
summary:
Pepper Advantage, a leading global credit intelligence and investment technology company, today announced that LendInvest plc (AIM: LINV), the UK alternative property finance platform, has selected its proprietary PRISM platform to power its credit management operations.
This agreement represents a pivotal milestone since the launch of PRISM. PRISM was built as Pepper Advantage's proprietary, AI-driven credit management ecosystem, and this partnership completes the platform's evolution into a commercially available SaaS solution for external market participants.
The decision follows a comprehensive review by LendInvest of technology providers across the credit and lending market. PRISM's credit workflow automation, customer portal and digital capabilities will support LendInvest's service-led, technology-enabled model, allowing the platform to scale efficiently as assets under management (AUM) grow. PRISM's real-time data analytics will also strengthen LendInvest's portfolio insight and risk management, providing earlier notice of emerging and potential risks.
The agreement builds upon a long-standing, successful relationship between Pepper Advantage and LendInvest, further solidifying their collaboration in the UK credit management sector.
Daniel O’Connor, Chief Operating Officer at LendInvest, said: “As LendInvest focuses on simplifying its operations and building a scalable platform, it’s clear AI tools can play a key role in enabling customer empathy and operational efficiency in how it manages loans throughout their lifecycle. PRISM was chosen for that purpose - to further enhance our service offering, reduce our loan-servicing costs, and provide valuable data to the business about portfolio performance”
Gary Stockley, Chief Product Officer at Pepper Advantage, said: “LendInvest’s selection of PRISM is a major validation of our technology and product vision. The platform’s commercial availability as a SaaS solution means we can bring its transformative capabilities to the wider market. LendInvest has been a long-standing partner of ours, and we are thrilled they have chosen PRISM to anchor their evolving operating model. We look forward to powering their credit management operations and supporting their next chapter of growth.”

content: Pepper Advantage announced that LendInvest has selected its proprietary PRISM platform to power its credit management operations. This partnership marks a key milestone in the commercial availability of PRISM as a SaaS solution, strengthening the long-standing relationship between the two companies as LendInvest enters its next growth phase.

10x Banking and ezbob Partner to Accelerate SME Lending Launches for Banks
summary:
10x Banking, the 4th-generation core banking platform powering some of the world’s largest financial institutions including Westpac and Chase UK, today announces a partnership with ezbob, a lending technology company who has worked with the likes of NatWest and Metro Bank. The partnership brings together ezbob’s lending-orchestration platform with 10x’s modular core and ledger to enable banks to launch SME lending products in weeks rather than months, and with less risk. 
SMEs are the backbone of the UK economy, accounting for 99.9% of all private businesses, yet SME lending remains one of the most persistent digital experience gaps in UK financial services. Incumbent banks have fully digitalised and automated simpler retail journeys such as current account onboarding and smaller personal loans, but SME lending is materially more complex. Attempts to close that gap have stalled because systems built on workflow tools or legacy cores move a process through internal steps without creating a connected customer journey, and become costly to operate. 
The new partnership sees ezbob provide the end-to-end lending solution, orchestrating onboarding, application, credit decisioning and AI agents. 10x provides the modular core and ledger capabilities needed to define and operate the lending product and maintain an accurate financial system of record. Open integration allows specialist components to be connected without forcing a bank into a single closed suite, and shared components can be reused to add further lending products rather than building a new silo each time. Overall, this will give banks the ability to launch new SME lending products in weeks rather than months, significantly reducing go-to-market and time-to-value. 
ezbob brings substantial experience in the segment. Lending products built on its platform have gone live in as little as six weeks, enabling 90%+ of applicants to complete an application in under five minutes and automating 94% of approvals. This, combined with the reusability of existing components and an AI-first deployment methodology, has enabled banks and financial institutions to further reduce time-to-market when launching subsequent products on the platform. 
The partnership starts in the UK, and in SME lending, where there is a wide digital experience gap. The companies intend this as the first step in a global partnership, extending to further markets and lending lines over time. 
Okan Ozaltin, Chief Product & Technology Officer, 10x Banking, said: “Banks are too often asked to choose between a broad suite that is difficult to adapt and a collection of point solutions that never quite connect. Neither gets a lender to market quickly. Bringing our core and ledger together with a specialist origination platform gives them a faster, lower-risk route to market, and the flexibility to keep evolving itafterwards. SME lending is where customers can get the most value, which is why we are starting there.” 
Yaron Shoshani, Chief Technology Officer, ezbob, said: “We built ezbob to digitise the lending journey itself, rather than automate an internal process on top of systems that were never designed for it. Pairing that with a tier-one bank-grade core means a lender can launch a complete SME product, automate decisions where policy allows, and reuse the same components to add further lending products instead of building a new silo each time.”

content: 10x Banking has partnered with ezbob to help banks launch SME lending products more quickly and with lower risk. The collaboration combines ezbob's lending-orchestration platform with 10x Banking's core and ledger systems. Initially focusing on the UK market, the partnership aims to bridge the digital experience gap in SME lending, enabling financial institutions to deploy new products in weeks rather than months.

Trust Payments Launches Virtual Cards for Travel Businesses, Powered by Weavr
summary:
Trust Payments, a leading fintech innovator across the UK and EU, has launched Virtual Cards for travel businesses, powered by embedded finance provider Weavr, helping eligible travel companies manage supplier payments with greater visibility and control. 
Trust Payments already supports travel businesses in accepting payments from their customers. Virtual Cards extend that relationship to the other side of the payment journey, enabling businesses to pay approved travel suppliers that accept Visa using single-use Visa virtual cards in GBP and EUR. The type of card offered will be Visa Commercial Choice Travel (VCCT), a virtual card solution purpose-built for commercial entities to handle automated supplier settlements and secure business travel payments.  
Each Virtual Card is linked to an individual booking, connecting booking and payment data so transactions are easier for finance teams to identify, track and reconcile. Businesses fund their account by bank transfer, with spending made from the available balance. 
Supplier failure remains a particular risk for the travel sector, but chargebacks can make a real difference: close to US$60 million has been recovered across 14 airline failures since 2017, according to 2025 industry research Protecting Travel Intermediaries. Though recovery isn’t guaranteed, booking data associated with each Virtual Card can help support chargeback claims if a supplier fails to deliver, subject to card scheme rules. Single-use card details cannot be reused, and payments are monitored in real time to help reduce fraud risk. 
Eligible supplier payments can also earn rebates paid by Trust Payments, helping travel businesses get more value from outgoing payments alongside faster and simpler reconciliation. Rebate rates vary depending on card and supplier type. 
Virtual Cards are available to eligible travel businesses in the UK and EEA, subject to business verification and anti-money laundering checks. 
Laurence Booth, Group CEO of Trust Payments, said: “Travel businesses have to manage money moving in both directions. We already support our customers in accepting payments from travellers and Virtual Cards mean we can now help them manage supplier payments too. By linking each supplier payment to an individual booking, we can give travel businesses clearer oversight of outgoing spend and reduce the manual work involved in reconciliation. Working with Weavr enables us to extend the payments relationship we already have with travel customers and support more of their payment journey.” 
Alex Mifsud, CEO and Co-Founder of Weavr, said: “Merchant acquirers already sit at the heart of the payments relationship with travel businesses. Embedded virtual card issuing gives them an opportunity to complement acquiring with supplier payments without having to build that capability from the ground up. By working with Trust Payments, we can bring these capabilities to travel businesses through a provider they already know, helping them gain greater visibility and control over how they pay suppliers.”

content: Trust Payments has launched Virtual Cards for travel businesses in the UK and EEA, powered by embedded finance provider Weavr. The solution uses single-use Visa virtual cards to help eligible travel companies manage supplier payments, improve reconciliation, reduce fraud risk, and earn rebates on outgoing transactions.

UK Adults Want Tax Cuts but not the Spending Cuts to Pay for Them
summary:
Taxd research finds 58 per cent of UK adults would cut council tax and half would cut VAT, but only a third would accept lower public spending to pay for it.
The post UK Adults Want Tax Cuts but not the Spending Cuts to Pay for Them appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Recent research by Taxd indicates that a majority of UK adults support tax cuts, including council tax and VAT. However, only a third are willing to accept the necessary public spending reductions required to fund them, highlighting a significant fiscal gap in public preferences.
